question: Do the smooth ACC and native ACC retain complete, collision-free scripted fixture completion during cut-in and stronger braking, and what comfort requests does SUMO override?
trigger: Sam requested continued bounded I-110 engineering without Hudson's unavailable policy.pt; the October 28 handoff explicitly calls for cut-in/hard/emergency braking tests.
status: Predeclared engineering tranche; no empirical or policy efficacy claim

acceptance.network: No collision, teleport, removal or unfinished trip after drain; fixed controlled through lanes and native tripinfo crosscheck
acceptance.event: Actor present for commands; cut-in must change physical lane and become agent_1's leader; braking actor must reach <=0.1 m/s and realize >=90% requested deceleration while agent_1 follows
acceptance.comfort: Report 2.05 m/s^3 engineering exceedances separately; never disable SUMO safety to satisfy comfort
acceptance.repeat: Canonical trace and event-journal hashes identical on one same-seed repeat
acceptance.matched: Byte-identical network, route demand and event specification within each seed/event pair; same passing and safety settings

no_event_check: One development-seed event-off run and a matched ordinary run must have identical trace hashes; disabled event adds no actor
failure_policy: Retain all runs; continue through acceptance failures, stop for infrastructure exceptions; do not retune this frozen tranche from its outcomes
limits: Synthetic traffic, two development-verification seeds, exact-state ACC. Emergency actor has a declared 9 m/s^2 braking capacity; this is not measured vehicle physics. Request mismatches do not identify SUMO's internal override cause. No real-world safety/comfort or traffic-benefit claim.
